AGAINST IULIANUM BOOK 1V Carnal lust is evil Resuwen-—Continues in this fourth book Julian's refutation, response to what he had written in his second book on Marriage and Lust, from the fourth to the eleventh chapter. Augustine strives to prove what he teaches in these passages when commenting on the text of the first letter of Saint John (c2,16): Everything that is in the world, the concupiscence of the flesh...—does not come from the Father. That is, the concupiscence of the flesh is evil, and cannot be the work of the Creator of human nature. It is, he says, natural in animals, but it was inflicted on the man as punishment. The modesty of the virile members took place after the sin, not before. Against Julian, he resolutely affirms that this concupiscence had no place in Christ my in its lesser degree and that children are born guilty of an original sin not by delusion of their own will, but by contagion of a sin voluntarily committed by our first father. Finally, it shows that the words of Wisdom: Knowing that it was a perverse race... (Wisdom 2,1011), can also serve to prove the sin of our origin.
